items.title: Beta Recall, Alpha Recall, and a Contamination Detector that Needs No Labels * Measuring Training-data Leakage in LLM Equity Signals
items.claim: LLM stock-ranking performance inside its training window is substantially recall-based rather than predictive.

items.title: Execution-Aware Alpha Mining: Teaching LLM Factor Agents to Account for Trading Costs​
items.claim: LLM alpha-mining agents optimized on gross returns converge to economically catastrophic turnover without explicit execution-cost penalties.

items.title: SoK: Trading Agents or Market Crashers? Dissecting Robustness and Security Failures in Academic Financial LLM Trading Schemes
items.claim: Every academic LLM trading agent scheme examined exhibits security vulnerabilities enabling low-cost market-crash attacks.

items.title: Why Discovery Layers Guarantee Crowded Alpha: A Design Case for Quality-Diversity Search in Agentic Trading Systems
items.claim: A discovery layer optimized purely for predictive quality is structurally guaranteed to converge on crowded factors.

items.title: A Three-Layer Reference Architecture for Deterministic Control in Agentic Trading Systems
items.claim: Three-layer architectures with hard-gated execution prevent documented agentic trading failures.

items.title: EvolveTrade: Experience-Driven Policy Refinement for Self-Evolving LLM Trading Agents
items.claim: System-prompt evolution using portfolio feedback improves LLM trading agents' Sharpe ratios in tested market regimes.
